newsitem.title: KUWAIT: Debt deadline, year-end hit Kuwait trade, index up.
newsitem.headline: Debt deadline, year-end hit Kuwait trade, index up.

text.p: Kuwait's share index edged up in the week to Wednesday despite a fall in volume and value ahead of a January bad debt repayment deadline for private investors, dealers said on Friday.
Anticipation over year-end results also cast a shadow over trade, they added.
The index rose 18.7 points to 1,887.9 points in the five-day week shortened to four trade days by a Moslem holiday, a weekly stock market report released on Thursday showed.
Gainers led losers 24-11 while 14 were non-movers.
"Debt repayment is one of the reasons (for the trade decline)," said private dealer Khalifa Jassem. "Dealers also want to see how the annual results are coming".
Private debtors involved in a programme to settle $20 billion in bad debt owed to the state have to pay a portion of their borrowings by January 7.
Trade has traditionally eased before debt payments.
"Some shares were boosted by talk about high year-end profits," said a portfolio manager.
Other portfolio managers, trying to show the highest profit possible in annual reports, are easing the pace, said dealer Mohammad al-Duhaishi.
"They are cautious. They do not want any transactions that could have a negative impact on their portfolios' profits at the end of the year."
Total value of traded shares eased to a daily average of 15.5 million dinars ($51.8 million) from 18.5 million dinars the previous week.
Volume fell to an average of 52.9 million shares per day from a daily average of 78 million shares a week earlier.
Banks were the most active sector in terms of traded value with 20.9 million dinars, followed by investment firms with 17.9 million and property with 16.7 million.
Commercial Bank, Gulf Bank, Investment Projects, the International Investor, United Realty, National Real Estate and Kuwait Real Estate were among the most active shares.
Only nationals of Gulf Arab states -- Saudi Arabia, Bahrain, United Arab Emirates, Qatar, Oman and Kuwait -- can trade on the exchange. Foreign residents can invest through mutual funds.
Kuwait is considering opening trade for foreign investors.
